title: Circular and Rotational Motion: Motion That Turns

questions.question: A body completes 2 full revolutions per second in a circle of radius 0.5 m. What is its angular velocity?
questions.rationale: One revolution is 2π rad, so ω = 2π × n = 2π × 2 = 4π rad/s.

questions.question: What supplies the centripetal force for a car taking a turn on a flat (unbanked) road?
options: Friction between the tyres and the road
The normal reaction of the road
questions.rationale: On a flat curve only friction points horizontally towards the centre of the turn, so friction plays the role of the centripetal force.

questions.question: Centripetal acceleration for a body moving with speed v in a circle of radius r is:
options: v²/r directed away from the centre
v/r² directed away from the centre
questions.rationale: The acceleration of uniform circular motion has magnitude v²/r and points radially inward, towards the centre of the circle.

questions.question: A skater spinning with arms extended pulls her arms in. What happens to her angular velocity, and why?
options: Increases — moment of inertia falls and angular momentum is conserved
Stays the same — speed is conserved
questions.rationale: With no external torque, L = Iω stays constant. Pulling the arms in reduces I, so ω must increase to compensate.

questions.question: The minimum speed at the top of a vertical circle of radius r for a body to complete the loop is:
questions.rationale: At the top, gravity alone can supply the whole centripetal force, so v² ≥ gr, giving v_min = √(gr).

questions.question: Which quantity is the rotational analogue of mass?
questions.rationale: Moment of inertia I = Σmr² resists changes in rotational motion, exactly as mass resists changes in straight-line motion.

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R about its diameter is:
questions.rationale: For a solid sphere about its symmetry axis, I = (2/5)MR². MR² is a ring and ½MR² is a disc.

questions.question: Why are roads banked at curves?
options: So a component of the normal reaction provides the centripetal force
questions.rationale: On a banked road the normal reaction tilts inward; its horizontal component supplies centripetal force, reducing reliance on friction.

questions.question: A 30 kg child sits 2 m from a see-saw's pivot. Where must a 60 kg adult sit to balance it?
questions.rationale: Rotational equilibrium needs equal moments: 30 × 2 = 60 × r, so r = 1 m.

questions.question: A geostationary satellite appears stationary above one point on Earth's equator because:
options: Its orbital period matches Earth's rotation period at an altitude of 35,786 km
Gravity does not act on it
It is stationary relative to the Sun
questions.rationale: At 35,786 km altitude the orbital period equals 24 hours, so the satellite revolves with the Earth and stays over the same longitude.
